The A1 dominance pass is a sub-pose margin that reverses held out. Frozen exact Bench(110,360), re-worn by this audit: plain 18.67 vs the lead's 18.91 (+0.24, i.e. 0.86 of one workspace pose at 0.278 points per pose); 2 mm 33.10 vs 34.03 (+0.93); 1 mm 20.30 vs 20.00 (-0.30). The whole plain gain is contact-pose count: 2 contact poses against 4 (contact 0.0054 vs 0.0107 = +0.53), offset by in-band14 0.8937 vs 0.8966 (-0.29). Reach is identical (261 of 360, overhead 8 of 28). Held out, with both designs re-worn through the same harness (alignment_audit remeasure): 23.73 vs 22.67 (-1.06; 851 vs 859 taken poses of 1154); 1 mm 26.83 vs 25.75 (-1.08); 2 mm 37.02 vs 37.24 (+0.22). Not gamed: at 3 mm this design is far ahead (107.65 vs 155.98 on the bench, 101.03 vs 163.09 held out; 133 vs 178 and 274 vs 427 poses under 3 mm). So the lead is not shown to be better for the wearer. But the gate's 'beats the lead' reading is noise, not a better exo, and it fails the 1-point rule. The drive sits at its transmission cap. The K stroke limit is set by the horn pressure angle (why_lim 'pressure_horn', dK_lim 46.2 deg). The taken dK reaches 45.62 deg, where the pressure angle reaches 43.0, exactly PA_MAX. That is the 2-degree cushion under the 45 gate, kept for the ~0.6 deg K slop and the flank tolerance. The tightest clearances are bent arm to hub K 1.14 mm and roller to hub K 2.02 mm. No force or dynamics check (R17) exists for this drive at that step, so the feel of a 43-degree roller-flank contact under K slop is unmeasured. The knee window walked toward the straight-knee singularity, but the score does not depend on it. ang_min has no bound anywhere in the model's _clamp chain, and the search moved it from the seed's 26.88 (the lead's verified value) to 25.22 (H1: 30.46). The taken knee angle runs to 151.92 deg on the bench and 153.16 held out, against the lead's 146.14 / 150.86: 5.8 deg closer to straight on the bench. Re-worn at the lead's ang_min 26.88, the result is identical (18.67 / 20.30 / 33.10), so the walk buys nothing against the lead. Re-worn at H1's 30.46: plain 18.71, 1 mm 20.36, 2 mm 36.76, reach 0.7167 (3 fewer poses), overhead 7 of 28. At that window it falls behind the lead at 2 mm. [evidence: docs/alignment/remeasure/roller-longdyad-knuckle-3r_angmin26.8823.json, docs/alignment/remeasure/roller-longdyad-knuckle-3r_angmin30.46.json, docs/alignment/live_audit_2026-10-16/probe_roller-longdyad-knuckle-3r_th.json (knee_ang_taken 86.21-151.92, window 25.22-154.78), remeasure _held.json coord_spans K.ang 86.21-153.16; docs/concepts/models/roller-longdyad-knuckle-3r.py:61-70]

K is scored at its planned (slaved) value, but it is held there by a single clock-spring cap that force-closes two rolling pairs: the lobe follower on hub 2's cap, and the MR63ZZ roller on the conjugate flank. The cam synthesis checks lift-off, cusp and pressure angles kinematically. No dynamics judge (R17) has run on this design, so nothing shows that the spring holds K on the law under arm load or gravity across the thorax. The new slaved-coordinate coupling in judge/dynamics.py (commits 5d6b819, 9f28755) is the instrument. This is required before any CAD, not before a screen. Paired per-pose re-wear by this audit (new tool tools/alignment_paired.py, models unchanged, farm, both designs on the same poses; the farm had no fast grid cache, so the fit-60 shape was fitted on exact distances - a perturbed fit, NOT the claim protocol): bench 19.34 vs 19.66 (roller better by 0.32; the equal reach hides 8 + 8 discordant poses), paired bootstrap SD 1.36, 90 % interval [-2.62, +1.77], P(roller better) 0.61; held out 24.28 vs 23.60 (lead better by 0.69; 21 vs 28 discordant poses, roller loses 18 vs 8 below elev 90 and wins 12 vs 9 at elev 90-140), 90 % [-0.80, +2.09], P(roller better) 0.23; pooled 22.90 vs 22.49 (lead better by 0.41), 90 % [-0.78, +1.61], P(roller better) 0.29. The perturbed fit alone moves each design by 0.67-0.92 points, 3x the margin, and the bench-vs-held sign flip reproduces under it. The deepest is the side wall of hub K's 18.25 mm stack (O20 + 6 mm spring cap) in the raised deltoid at elevation 150-165 (red team cluster A; lifting the hub 7 mm moves it only to -14.23), and the knee link and pad 10 mm into the chest wall with the arm across the body (cluster C). Contact plus near-touch under 1 mm, held out: 36 vs 29 poses. R1-aim (in-band 2-10) held out 0.563 vs 0.593 (fit-60), 0.497 vs 0.574 (env). Every contact pose is already counted as not reached plus its share, so the number is not inflated by them; but a 14.6 mm press into the deltoid and a 0.1 mm graze cost the same. Not gamed: no clip frame touches, and BDp does not close 19 of pick1's 28 env-fit contact poses at all. reason_items.reason: The round-9 'win by 0.24' is not a measurable gain: it is a tie inside the bench's own sampling noise, and the larger held-out set leans the other way. Claim protocol (fit-60 fast shape, worn exact; re-worn to the digit 2026-10-16 and unchanged since: same best_params): bench 18.67 vs the lead's 18.91 (+0.24 = 2 fewer contact poses +0.53, in-band -0.29, reach equal 261/360); held out 23.73 vs 22.67 (lead better by 1.06: 649 vs 657 of 952 reached, 10 vs 10 contact poses, in-band -0.21); pooled bench+held (1312 workspace poses, from the files) about 22.3 vs 21.6, lead better by ~0.7. Paired per-pose re-wear by this audit (new tool tools/alignment_paired.py, models unchanged, farm, both designs on the same poses; the farm had no fast grid cache, so the fit-60 shape was fitted on exact distances - a perturbed fit, NOT the claim protocol): bench 19.34 vs 19.66 (roller better by 0.32; the equal reach hides 8 + 8 discordant poses), paired bootstrap SD 1.36, 90 % interval [-2.62, +1.77], P(roller better) 0.61; held out 24.28 vs 23.60 (lead better by 0.69; 21 vs 28 discordant poses, roller loses 18 vs 8 below elev 90 and wins 12 vs 9 at elev 90-140), 90 % [-0.80, +2.09], P(roller better) 0.23; pooled 22.90 vs 22.49 (lead better by 0.41), 90 % [-0.78, +1.61], P(roller better) 0.29. The perturbed fit alone moves each design by 0.67-0.92 points, 3x the margin, and the bench-vs-held sign flip reproduces under it. Not gamed: the lead is more likely better on the score out of sample (P 0.71-0.77) but not decisively (every 90 % interval contains 0), and this design is simpler (complexity 43.75 vs 49) with far fewer poses at 2-3 mm, so no measured proof that the lead is better for the wearer. Under the 2026-10-17 rule (plain verified gap decides) the label 'winner' follows mechanically, but it rests on noise: report it as a tie / complexity Pareto point, and do not take its 0.24 as progress toward 95. [evidence: docs/alignment/remeasure/roller-longdyad-knuckle-3r_vs_sidecar-longdyad-knuckle-3r_paired_exactfit.json; docs/alignment/remeasure/{roller,sidecar}-longdyad-knuckle-3r_{bench,held}_perpose.json; docs/alignment/remeasure/roller-longdyad-knuckle-3r_bench.json, _held.json, sidecar-longdyad-knuckle-3r_bench.json; docs/alignment/live_audit_2026-10-16/ref_sidecar-longdyad-knuckle-3r_held_same_harness.json; docs/concepts/ROUNDS.md 'Round 9 results']

The sample-weighted in-band rewards added metal area, and that alone moves this design by half its margin. The verifier's envelope correction ADDS 19 metal points that exist on the real part (9 on the O5 roller head, 10 on the lug flank-edge strip) and the gap IMPROVES from 18.67 to 18.56 (in-band14 0.8937 -> 0.8948), because the added points sit in band. Making the model more real should never be a gain. The claim correctly stays at 18.67, but ROUNDS.md 'Round 9 results' prints 'envelope-corrected 18.56' beside the winner. The drive sits at its transmission cap. The K stroke limit is the horn pressure angle (why_lim 'pressure_horn', dK_lim 46.25 deg); the taken dK reaches 45.62 deg where the pressure angle is 43.0 (= PA_MAX, the 2-degree cushion under the 45 gate kept for ~0.6 deg K slop and flank tolerance; the verifier reads 42.7). Tightest clearances: bent arm to hub K 1.14 mm, roller to hub K 2.02 mm. Under the 2026-10-17 kinematic-proof ruling this stays a geometric margin; it is the posture where a small K error stiffens the drive. [evidence: docs/concepts/verify/roller-longdyad-knuckle-3r_v_bench_frozen.json fit_fast.extra (pa_horn_max 43.0, dK_lim_deg 46.25, why_lim pressure_horn); row verification.drive (pa_horn_max 42.7, dK_taken_max 45.62); docs/concepts/models/roller-longdyad-knuckle-3r.py:45]

K is scored at its slaved value and held there by one clock-spring cap that force-closes two rolling pairs (lobe follower on hub 2's cap; MR63ZZ roller on the conjugate flank). The verifier checks closure kinematically (closure 0.0 mm, roller never inside the lug, K sense always the drive's). Nothing shows the spring keeps both pairs closed under arm load; the lead's RSSR shares the same clock-spring cap, so this does not rank the two. Kept as watch for MVP1 / CAD, not a metric (2026-10-17 ruling: all checks stay kinematic). [evidence: docs/concepts/rows/roller-longdyad-knuckle-3r.json mechanism (springs_or_flexures 1, rolling_pairs 2, notes 'K slaved (clock-spring cap), never read') and verification.drive; no dynamics output for this id]

Under the user's 2026-10-17 ruling ('a sensed joint is a joint'), this design's mechanism record still lists its 2 knee pins as 'sensed_passive' and the complexity check calls them cuff-side passives outside the count: 3 active + 2 sensed = 5 read coordinates, 4 O20 hubs in the shoulder chain (K slaved by the cam, not read). The cuff-side exemption in CLAUDE.md names passive self-aligning slides; whether two encoded knee pins stay outside the DOF count is not covered by the ruling. It does not change roller vs lead (identical pin knee) and complexity is recomputed equal (43.75); it is a question for the user that every knuckle-family row shares. The user ruled on 2026-10-17 that a sensed joint is a joint ('Sensed 4 joint does not count as passive obviously'). This design's mechanism record keeps the pin knee's 2 encoder-read pins as sensed_passive 2 (5 points each) outside the DOF count, as cuff-side self-aligning freedoms (CLAUDE.md 2026-10-15: passive self-aligning freedoms at the cuff are outside the count). ROUNDS.md round 6 already lists this asymmetry (a sensed K counts as active, the knee's sensed pins as passive) as needing the user's say. Measured with tools/simplicity.py: if the 2 sensed knee pins counted as joints, this design would be 5 DOF (over the cap of 4) and complexity 49 -> 87. The same holds for every pin-knee row: roller-longdyad 43.75 -> 81.75, parallelogram 49 -> 87, roller-flank 45.25 -> 83.25, frontload 49 -> 87, all 5 DOF. Only the kneeless rows (21.07 / 21.11, 0 sensed) would stay 3-joint designs within the cap. Not gamed: the cuff-side rule is an explicit user ruling and the 2026-10-17 quote names the shoulder-chain 4th joint; the ranking among the pin-knee rows does not change. Under the user's 2026-10-17 ruling (a sensed joint is a joint) this is a 4-joint design: at the DOF cap, not the preferred 3. Its plain lead over the 3-joint rows is one to two workspace poses (one workspace pose = 0.278 gap points), and under the same held-out protocol and at 1 mm it does not lead. Plain: pick1 18.40 vs roller-longdyad 18.67 (+0.27) and sidecar-longdyad 18.91 (+0.51). Held out (fit Bench(60,160) -> the 1154 held-out poses, exact): pick1 22.69 vs sidecar-parallelogram 22.03, sidecar-longdyad 22.67, roller-longdyad 23.73. Near-touch 1 mm, bench: 23.36 vs 20.22 / 20.00 / 20.30; held out: 26.73 vs 24.44 / 25.75 / 26.83. The 4th joint buys 9 more workspace poses on the bench (reach 0.750 vs sidecar-longdyad 0.725), none of them overhead (overhead workspace taken 7 of 28 vs 8 of 28), and costs contact (contact share 0.0281 vs 0.0107; 11 vs 4 bench poses with metal inside the skin, deepest -13.17 vs -4.61 mm). README still heads the status with 'Best verified overall: minarc pick1 18.40'. Not gamed: it reaches more of the workspace, no 3-joint row is better on every measure, and the user's ruling already makes the 3-joint rows the leaders. The polish that replaced BDp as the row's number and as the CAD config (pick1: 19.54 -> 18.40 on the bench, 24.18 -> 22.69 held out) takes FEWER overhead poses. Overhead workspace (elevation >= 140) taken: bench 7 of 28 vs BDp 8; held out with the fit-60 shape 12 of 71 vs 16; with the env-fit shape 16 vs 17. Its gain is total reach at mid and low elevation (held-out reach 0.7195 vs 0.6828, about 35 workspace poses). The polish note says 'the overhead grid nodes rise from 32 to 44': that counts kinematic closures, while the overhead poses the wearer actually takes (closed, no contact, connected) fall. The gap weighs every workspace pose equally, so it books an overhead loss paid by mid-range gains as a gain; the goal puts overhead first. Re-worn here (bench): pick1 loses 5 overhead workspace poses to contact against BDp's 2 (held out 16 vs 7), and K is closed on every taken pose at elevation >= 140 (bench 0 of 7 workspace poses and 0 of 10 clip frames; held out 0 of 12 and 0 of 19; K opens on 86 / 209 lower poses): the 4th joint does nothing overhead. The user ruled the score stays as is for overhead (2026-10-16), so this is reported, not scored. Not gamed: BDp reaches about 35 fewer held-out workspace poses, so it is not better for the wearer on every axis. [evidence: docs/alignment/remeasure/minarc-stop-knuckle-4r_{pick1,BDp}_probe_bench.json (K_open_by_elev, probe.ws_overhead_why_not); docs/research/minarc_final_polish/verify/v_pick1_fit60_bench.json, v_BDp_fit60_bench.json, v_pick1_fit60_held.json, v_BDp_fit60_held.json, v_pick1_env_held.json, v_BDp_env_held.json (overhead140_ws); docs/research/minarc_final_polish.md line 237]

The contact term counts poses with metal inside the skin by share, not by depth, and the in-band term never samples hub K's cap. pick1's extra reach comes with more and deeper contact on the poses next to it. Contact poses: bench 11 vs BDp 4 (deepest -13.17 vs -6.41 mm, both overhead at elevation 165); held out, fit-60 shape 35 vs 13 (deepest -14.61 vs -7.27 mm); env-fit shape 28 vs 9 (-14.58 vs -7.27). The deepest is the side wall of hub K's 18.25 mm stack (O20 + 6 mm spring cap) in the raised deltoid at elevation 150-165 (red team cluster A; lifting the hub 7 mm moves it only to -14.23), and the knee link and pad 10 mm into the chest wall with the arm across the body (cluster C). Contact plus near-touch under 1 mm, held out: 36 vs 29 poses. R1-aim (in-band 2-10) held out 0.563 vs 0.593 (fit-60), 0.497 vs 0.574 (env). Every contact pose is already counted as not reached plus its share, so the number is not inflated by them; but a 14.6 mm press into the deltoid and a 0.1 mm graze cost the same. Not gamed: no clip frame touches, and BDp does not close 19 of pick1's 28 env-fit contact poses at all. DETERMINACY without the knee encoders HOLDS for this design, under one condition: K must stay on its law. This was re-run on this design, model and verifier unchanged, with the frozen protocol and the null-space Jacobian of the loop J1-K-J2-J3-pin a-pin b-GH(3R). Frames were checked from both members of every joint (max error 7e-6 mm). With K slaved by its lin law (slope dK/dq2 = 1.6232 regressed from the taken poses, residual 0.0; 0 on stop A), mobility is 3 at every taken pose. The 3 hub rates fix every passive coordinate, the knee pins and GH included. Exact Bench(110,360), frozen (gap reproduced 18.91; 375 taken poses, 123 with K open, 252 on stop A): hub sigma_min min 0.310, p5 0.311, median 0.553; condition max 2.80; knee-pin rate per hub rate up to 2.34 (median 0.43). The fit bench (188 poses) gives the same: 0.310 / 2.75. Reference skin-normal-3r-pin-knee: sigma_min >= 0.39, condition <= 2.3, so this design is a little worse conditioned but nowhere near singular (0 poses under 0.05). The condition: with K free (no law), mobility is 4 and the hub encoders alone have sigma_min 0 at every pose. A K lag or drive lift-off is then invisible to the 3 encoders and goes straight into the estimated arm pose. K is held on its law only by one 0.08 N.m clock spring keeping the drive in compression, and R17 (lift-off / K lag) has never run on this design (M5). So 'no encoders needed' is proven at the kinematic level only, not for the real spring-held drive. Not gamed: the premise holds at every taken pose in the model. This was re-run on this design, model and verifier unchanged, with the frozen protocol and the null-space Jacobian of the loop J1-K-J2-J3-pin a-pin b-GH(3R). Frames were checked from both members of every joint (max error 7e-6 mm). With K slaved by its lin law (slope dK/dq2 = 1.6232 regressed from the taken poses, residual 0.0; 0 on stop A), mobility is 3 at every taken pose. The 3 hub rates fix every passive coordinate, the knee pins and GH included. Exact Bench(110,360), frozen (gap reproduced 18.91; 375 taken poses, 123 with K open, 252 on stop A): hub sigma_min min 0.310, p5 0.311, median 0.553; condition max 2.80; knee-pin rate per hub rate up to 2.34 (median 0.43). The fit bench (188 poses) gives the same: 0.310 / 2.75. Reference skin-normal-3r-pin-knee: sigma_min >= 0.39, condition <= 2.3, so this design is a little worse conditioned but nowhere near singular (0 poses under 0.05). The condition: with K free (no law), mobility is 4 and the hub encoders alone have sigma_min 0 at every pose. A K lag or drive lift-off is then invisible to the 3 encoders and goes straight into the estimated arm pose. K is held on its law only by one 0.08 N.m clock spring keeping the drive in compression, and R17 (lift-off / K lag) has never run on this design (M5). So 'no encoders needed' is proven at the kinematic level only, not for the real spring-held drive. Not gamed: the premise holds at every taken pose in the model. [evidence: tools/alignment_knee_determinacy.py (new); docs/alignment/remeasure/sidecar-longdyad-knuckle-3r_knee_determinacy_bench.json (exact) and the fit-bench pass (Bench(60,160), fast); reference docs/concepts/skin-normal-3r-pin-knee.md lines 565-568; M5 below]

DETERMINACY without the knee encoders HOLDS for this design, under one condition: K must stay on its law. This was re-run on this design, model and verifier unchanged, with the frozen protocol and the null-space Jacobian of the loop J1-K-J2-J3-pin a-pin b-GH(3R). Frames were checked from both members of every joint (max error 7e-6 mm). With K slaved by its lin law (slope dK/dq2 = 1.6232 regressed from the taken poses, residual 0.0; 0 on stop A), mobility is 3 at every taken pose. The 3 hub rates fix every passive coordinate, the knee pins and GH included. Exact Bench(110,360), frozen (gap reproduced 18.91; 375 taken poses, 123 with K open, 252 on stop A): hub sigma_min min 0.310, p5 0.311, median 0.553; condition max 2.80; knee-pin rate per hub rate up to 2.34 (median 0.43). The fit bench (188 poses) gives the same: 0.310 / 2.75. Reference skin-normal-3r-pin-knee: sigma_min >= 0.39, condition <= 2.3, so this design is a little worse conditioned but nowhere near singular (0 poses under 0.05). The condition: with K free (no law), mobility is 4 and the hub encoders alone have sigma_min 0 at every pose. A K lag or drive lift-off is then invisible to the 3 encoders and goes straight into the estimated arm pose. K is held on its law only by one 0.08 N.m clock spring keeping the drive in compression, and R17 (lift-off / K lag) has never run on this design (M5). So 'no encoders needed' is proven at the kinematic level only, not for the real spring-held drive. Not gamed: the premise holds at every taken pose in the model. [evidence: tools/alignment_knee_determinacy.py (new); docs/alignment/remeasure/sidecar-longdyad-knuckle-3r_knee_determinacy_bench.json (exact) and the fit-bench pass (Bench(60,160), fast); reference docs/concepts/skin-normal-3r-pin-knee.md lines 565-568; M5 below]

The dip is a spring-closed cam. One clock spring must close K below the old stop A into a lobe dip 0.068 mm deep and hold it on the law, while it also force-closes the roller-flank. No spring torque, closure force or friction check exists for this row. The row's mechanism notes say 'watch: unproven spring-closed cam', and there is no dynamics (R17) run. If the follower lifts on a dipped pose, K is free between the dip floor and the lobe. On those poses the J1-K-J3 sub-chain sits 0.18-0.20 deg from its fold (see T3). K is never read: the pose comes from the hub encoders only. [evidence: row mechanism.notes; row frozen.drive dK_dip_taken -2.37; verification.drive lobe_dip_mm 0.068]

The feature that makes the number is smaller than a machining tolerance. The lobe dip is 0.068 mm deep. The verifier measured that 10 um of lobe profile error is 0.35 deg of K, against a 2.37 deg dip floor (15 %). The two recovered bench poses ride on that feature; pose 203 sits at 0.48 mm. With stop A moved to the dip floor, K's rest through the whole dwell now sits on the drive chain (lobe -> bell crank -> bent 3 mm Ti arm -> MR63ZZ roller -> flank) instead of a dowel stop. So the chain's tolerance stack sets K everywhere, not only in the dip. The model treats the profile as exact. [evidence: row verification.issues[0], verification.drive K_deg_per_10um_lobe 0.35; model header ('Stop A moves to the dip floor, and the lobe holds K at its old rest angle through the dwell')]

The drive works at its limits. This is inherited from the lead and tightened by the dip. The horn pressure angle is 43.0 deg, at the 43 deg cap: K is taken to 43.66 deg of a dK_lim of 43.8 (why_lim pressure_horn). The bent arm clears hub K by 1.04 mm at the dip floor, against the 1 mm rule, and closes 0.18 mm per deg past it. The dip itself spends stretched stroke: dK_lim falls from 46.2 to 43.8. [evidence: row frozen.drive; verification.drive; docs/concepts/dipped-law-groove-knuckle-3r.md]

judgement:M5: A spring that may not hold, now against sliding friction (not measured). One clock spring (0.08 N.m + 0.03 N.m/rad, the lead's) force-closes the lobe follower and, here, a SLIDING nose instead of the lead's rolling MR63ZZ. On the return stroke the spring drives the crank through the horn at a crank pressure angle of 29.5 deg kinematic + 4.97 deg friction = 34.47 deg (the lead's crank side: 8.2 deg, rolling). The score assumes K on its cam law at all 167 bench / 400 held-out taken poses where K moves. No R17 / dynamics / preload number is on file for this design; the only evidence is the claim's hand calculation (friction drag ~0.01-0.02 N.m against the 0.08 N.m preload). Held out, worn here through the verifier's own --truewin protocol: 28.77 vs bench 22.64 (+6.13, above the +6 watch line; before this re-wear the tool's held_out check read the claim's refuted 24.96 from row.held_out and said +2.32 ok; the verifier's dropped-pose correction says 28.90, +6.26). The cause is not in-sample tuning: the search moved only the drive (seats are the lead's), and stop B at 32.25 deg cuts more held-out poses (37 past the window in the claim wear) than bench poses (12) because the held-out set reaches deeper K. The claim's 19.29 was bought by closed-form gates in a simplified geometry: the groove-fit gate was planar and linear (crest 8.24 at dK 41.25) while the crank turns about an axis tilted 14.78 deg from hub 2's and the dowel drifts 15.6 deg, so the TRUE crest was 8.93 against the claim's own 8.44 window (a 0.31-mm outer wall instead of 0.8): worth 3.35 points (19.29 -> 22.64). The same simplification put the groove pressure angle at 30.5 deg; in 3-D it is 36.17 against a 37.29 gate. The verifier corrected the number, so the 22.64 no longer depends on it; the pattern is not in the catalogue (proposal M6). The lead's rim lobe follower turns about the same tilted crank axis; whether its lobe crest / pressure angle carry the same planar error has not been checked. [evidence: docs/concepts/verify/groove-desmo-knuckle-3r_v_bench_frozen.json groove (pitch_r_grid 8.934, window 8.44, crank_axis_tilt 14.78, pa_groove_3d 36.17); row verification.finding]

A catalogue part used at a size where it cannot work: the verified 22.64 is worn with a 1.52-wide groove and a straight ISO 8734 O1.5 dowel, but the dowel tilts up to 4.2 deg across the rise groove (3.3 deg at the cut stroke): 0.108 mm (0.085) of run-out over the 1.5-mm engagement against 0.02 mm of clearance, so it binds (verifier). Fix 1, a 1.59-1.61 groove, narrows the pitch window from both sides and moves stop B earlier. MEASURED here (tools/alignment_groove_width_probe.py, new; model constants patched in memory only, verifier --truewin): with the 1.61 groove the window is [7.105, 8.395], stop B 30.75 deg, Bench(110,360) exact frozen gap 23.77 (reach 0.6694) vs the verified 22.64 (docs/alignment/remeasure/groove-desmo-knuckle-3r_groove1.61_bench.json). That is 4 more lost workspace poses (reach 0.6806 -> 0.6694) and puts the design behind frontload (22.82) on the plain gap, where today it is ahead by 0.18. Fix 2, a crowned dowel, is a made part (+0.25 complexity) and keeps the 1.52 window, so 22.64 by construction (not re-worn). [evidence: docs/concepts/verify/groove-desmo-knuckle-3r_v_bench_frozen.json groove (tilt 4.17, runout 0.108, width needed 1.613); _truewin.json (1.59, slop 1.62)]

The complexity edge (18.25 vs the lead's 20.25) is smaller than the count says. tools/simplicity.py's own sliding weight is 'each track pair (rail, carriage, arc track, sleeve on a rod, slot)', but the record counts the closed two-walled roller SLOT at K as a rolling pair (0 points), while the project's own records of a roller in a slot count it as a sliding pair (cam-coupled-4r: MR63 roller in a 6.1-mm slot, slotted-eccentric-j2-3r: MR52 roller in a 2.6-mm slot, sliding_pairs 1 each); a single roller in a closed slot with clearance also reverses spin at every wall change and skids. Counted as a track pair: 19.25 (edge 1.0). With a crowned dowel: +0.25; with the true bought count 14 (the record rounds up to 15): -0.25. Range 18.0-19.5, still simpler than the lead. The knee-template over-subtraction found on the lead's record (roller-longdyad G5) is copied here unchanged, so it shifts both rows alike. [evidence: python3 tools/simplicity.py score on the row's mechanism with sliding_pairs 2 / rolling_pairs 0 -> 19.25; custom +1 bought -1 -> 18.5; bought 14 -> 18.0; lead 20.25]

A held coordinate scored at its planned value: the bench evaluates K exactly on its law, but the positive drive holds it only to +-1.6-2.0 deg (the groove a straight dowel needs; the claim said +-0.54). K is slaved and never read, so this slop is also an unread 2-deg error in the hub-only pose estimate. It is a milder form of the lead's M5 (spring drift 4-8 deg), so the design is better than the lead here, but the effect of the slop on metal distance and on the pose estimate is not measured. [evidence: docs/concepts/verify/groove-desmo-knuckle-3r_v_bench_frozen.json groove slop_K_deg_needed 2.03 (1.62 at the cut stroke); row note]

A drive near friction lock: the groove's true 3-D pressure angle is 36.17 deg against a gate of 43 - atan(mu) = 37.29 with mu 0.1 assumed (a greased hardened pair). The gate passes only for mu <= 0.12 (tan 6.83 deg); dry hardened steel at mu 0.15 gives a 34.5-deg gate, which 36.17 fails. A drive that stiffens when the grease goes is something the wearer feels. The horn side is better than the lead's (39.0 at the cut stroke vs the lead's 43.0 = PA_MAX). [evidence: docs/concepts/verify/groove-desmo-knuckle-3r_v_bench_frozen_truewin.json groove pa_groove_3d_taken_max 36.17, pa_groove_gate 37.29; roller pa_horn_max 39.0]

Unchecked part interfaces: the 3-mm short arm runs at link 1b's plate level inside hub 2's footprint and needs a pocket in link 1b that no model or verifier checks (the parent's rim-lobe follower has the same); the groove's onset corner (the lin law's kink, ~85 deg in the cap frame) needs a blended onset that is not modelled (< 1 deg of K, per the claim). [evidence: docs/concepts/groove-desmo-knuckle-3r.md 'Not on the bench, but corrects the claim'; row note (red team)]

Not worse than the lead; still metal in the arm overhead. [evidence: docs/alignment/remeasure/groove-desmo-knuckle-3r_bench_probe.json, _held_probe.json contact_poses; _perpose.json]

A metal-deleted attribution is cited as beating the leader and handed on as the ceiling to chase. LS_GHOST (docs/concepts/models/longstroke-slipper-knuckle-3r.py _ghost, lines 127-135) deletes the drive's crank, rod, ball links and horn lug as in-band samples, as skin-contact samples (members 8 and 9 and the horn's member-1 entry) and as per-pose part pairs (strap ROD / CRK / HORN, so the sidecar collide() skips its ~18 drive pairs). It KEEPS the drive's range scan (transmission >= 48, ROD-hub2 / ROD-L1b / CRK-hub2 at 1 mm; it runs before the deletion: dK_lim 73.0, why 'law'), the lobe law gates (PA <= 42, skirt: crest 10.87 of 11.5 mm, lift-off, stop B) and the th fold margin (5.389 bench / 5.28 held). So it deletes metal, not kinematic constraints. Re-worn here, model unchanged, exact: 18.25 bench / 21.10 held, reproduced (remeasure/longstroke-ghost-k30_{bench,held}_perpose.json). The same config with its metal measures 25.83 on the bench (farm claimG real_k30: in-band 0.897 -> 0.859, contact 7 -> 14 poses, deepest 14.7 mm, overhead 8 -> 5 of 28). Part pairs did not bind there (why.parts 0). The same config with metal was never worn held out, so the deleted pair checks are unmeasured on the 952 poses. The number is a ceiling only for a drive that reproduces THIS rod's phi(dK) map (ratio dphi/ddK 0.558-0.653). The lobe's pressure angle scales with that gain, so a drive with another gain must re-check kK 3.0. It is a loose ceiling on in-band: a drive whose own metal is mostly in band could gain up to 0.31 points. Its continuity (flood) was never measured, and the row's nose control (18.49 reproduced) runs the nose branch: it does not exercise the rssr or LS_GHOST path. Not gaming: the row labels it ATTRIBUTION ONLY. The risk is downstream: the number travels as 'held 2.34 better than slipper-nose' without these limits. [evidence: model lines 116, 127-135; docs/concepts/models/sidecar-longdyad-knuckle-3r.py lines 196-249 (range scan before deletion, collide returns early without CRK); docs/alignment/remeasure/longstroke-ghost-k30_bench_perpose.json, _held_perpose.json; docs/research/longstroke_drive/farm/claimG/real_k30_bench.json; row claims.control_slipper_at_pa42]

Held-out leakage in the attribution's law choice. The steep law (kK 3.0, s_arm 4.0, r_lobe 8.5) was set by hand after the ghost fit (g65d: kK 1.977, s_arm 5.69, r_lobe 7.61). It was picked from a law-only table counted on Bench(110,360) AND the 952 held-out poses (docs/research/longstroke_drive/stroke_curve.py line 24 calls held_bench(); research note section 8: 267 -> 273 bench, 671 -> 689 held). The frozen protocol's fit bench does not see the gain: fit_fast 12.23 -> 12.12 (-0.11). The claim bench sees 19.50 -> 18.25 (-1.25) and held out 22.69 -> 21.11 (-1.58) (farm claimD / claimG). The pick is the model gate's boundary (kK 3.4 dies) and also the claim-bench best, so the leak is one choice among ~6 laws, not a search. Even so, 21.11 is not a clean held-out number, and '2.34 better held out' is not frozen-protocol evidence. [evidence: docs/research/longstroke_drive/stroke_curve.py; docs/research/longstroke_drive.md section 8; farm claimD/ghost_g65d_*.json fit_fast 12.23, claimG/ghost_k30_*.json fit_fast 12.12]

Where the held-out gain lives (paired, per pose, exact; tools/alignment_paired.py compare). Bench: ghost -0.24 vs slipper-nose, 90 % CI [-2.12, +1.85], P(ghost better) 0.55: a coin toss. The ghost takes 8 workspace poses slipper-nose does not and loses 3. Overhead is 8 / 28 for both. Contact poses rise 2 -> 7. 4 of the 5 contact-only poses are low-arm and internally rotated (plane -90 to -60, elev 45-60, axial +105 to +135; deepest 7.1 mm), and slipper-nose takes 2 of them cleanly. Held out, 6 of 7 contact-only poses are in the same class, and slipper-nose takes 5 of them cleanly. Held out: -2.35, CI [-3.70, -0.86], P 0.997: statistically robust. The ghost takes 30 poses slipper-nose does not and loses 5. Of the 30, 17 are at elevation < 60 and 6 at 60-90; 16 have |axial| >= 120. Only 4 are at 90-140 and 3 overhead (21 vs 18 of 71). So the held-out gain comes mostly from low-arm, extreme-axial poses that the 360-pose bench samples thinly. It does not come from the stretched th 110-113 poses the long stroke and steep law were for. Split by attribution: a new held dump of ghost g65d (kK 1.98, the same chain; remeasure/longstroke-ghost-g65d_held_perpose.json, 22.69 reproduced). The long-dyad chain at the CMA's law already takes +14 poses vs slipper-nose (0 lost): 9 below elevation 90 and the 3 overhead ones. The steep law kK 3.0 adds 17 more and loses 6. All 11 of the 17 that sit below elevation 60 have |axial| >= 120 (extreme rotation, arm low); 3 are at 90-140 and 0 overhead. It also adds 7 contact poses: 6 are shallow (0.2-2.0 mm) in the low-arm, internally rotated class (plane -90 to -15, elev 45-75, axial +90 to +105), and g65d took 5 of them cleanly. It also deepens the (-90, 60, 120) press from 6.1 to 9.2 mm. So kK 3.0's held-out 1.58 buys extreme-rotation postures with the arm low, and 0 of the 71 overhead poses. [evidence: docs/alignment/remeasure/longstroke-ghost-k30_vs_slipper-nose-knuckle-3r_paired.json; _classes.json]

A stiffer spring feel at the steep law, unmeasured (also M5). The lobe follower is force-closed by K's clock spring (0.08 N.m + 0.015 N.m/rad, row red_team.liftoff). The wearer feels kK x tau_K at J2. Claim (kK 1.957): 0.18 N.m, 1.2-1.5 N at a 120-150 mm cuff. Ghost law (kK 3.0, K used 54.0 deg = 0.94 rad): 3.0 x (0.08 + 0.015 x 0.94) = 0.28 N.m, 1.9-2.35 N at 150-120 mm: within 0.15 N of the 2.5 N line at a 120 mm cuff, and over it for a lever under 113 mm. K also turns 3x as fast as q2, so the follower's dynamic hold (lift-off under the chain's inertia) matters more. No R17 / dynamics run exists for kK 3.0. [evidence: row red_team.liftoff; row claims.steep_law_k30 dK_taken_max 51.75 / 53.97]

Partly idle stroke on the claim (s65n2d). The drive's range is 65.0 deg. The re-worn bench (exact, model unchanged) records K over taken poses spanning -0.7265 rad = 41.63 deg. That confirms the row's 41.62 and the 'taken poses use 41.6 deg of K' reading. Held out (re-worn, 26.19 reproduced): 41.52 deg. Slipper-nose, the short-stroke leader, uses 45.6 deg on the bench and 46.3 held (remeasure coord_spans). So the long-stroke claim uses 4 deg LESS K than the design it was meant to beat. 23.4 deg of its 65-deg stroke (36 %) is idle on every taken pose, and it pays +8.25 complexity (30.5 vs 22.25). Its cma3 constraint 'stroke >= 65' was met vacuously. The row says this itself, and the claim ranks behind the reference, so nothing is ranked above a better design. [evidence: docs/alignment/remeasure/longstroke-slipper-knuckle-3r_bench.json deep.coord_spans.dK; docs/alignment/remeasure/slipper-nose-knuckle-3r_{bench,held}.json deep.coord_spans.dK]

judgement:S1: Where the held-out gain lives (paired, per pose, exact; tools/alignment_paired.py compare). Bench: ghost -0.24 vs slipper-nose, 90 % CI [-2.12, +1.85], P(ghost better) 0.55: a coin toss. The ghost takes 8 workspace poses slipper-nose does not and loses 3. Overhead is 8 / 28 for both. Contact poses rise 2 -> 7. 4 of the 5 contact-only poses are low-arm and internally rotated (plane -90 to -60, elev 45-60, axial +105 to +135; deepest 7.1 mm), and slipper-nose takes 2 of them cleanly. Held out, 6 of 7 contact-only poses are in the same class, and slipper-nose takes 5 of them cleanly. Held out: -2.35, CI [-3.70, -0.86], P 0.997: statistically robust. The ghost takes 30 poses slipper-nose does not and loses 5. Of the 30, 17 are at elevation < 60 and 6 at 60-90; 16 have |axial| >= 120. Only 4 are at 90-140 and 3 overhead (21 vs 18 of 71). So the held-out gain comes mostly from low-arm, extreme-axial poses that the 360-pose bench samples thinly. It does not come from the stretched th 110-113 poses the long stroke and steep law were for. Split by attribution: a new held dump of ghost g65d (kK 1.98, the same chain; remeasure/longstroke-ghost-g65d_held_perpose.json, 22.69 reproduced). The long-dyad chain at the CMA's law already takes +14 poses vs slipper-nose (0 lost): 9 below elevation 90 and the 3 overhead ones. The steep law kK 3.0 adds 17 more and loses 6. All 11 of the 17 that sit below elevation 60 have |axial| >= 120 (extreme rotation, arm low); 3 are at 90-140 and 0 overhead. It also adds 7 contact poses: 6 are shallow (0.2-2.0 mm) in the low-arm, internally rotated class (plane -90 to -15, elev 45-75, axial +90 to +105), and g65d took 5 of them cleanly. It also deepens the (-90, 60, 120) press from 6.1 to 9.2 mm. So kK 3.0's held-out 1.58 buys extreme-rotation postures with the arm low, and 0 of the 71 overhead poses. Re-worn here through the verifier harness, unchanged: 22.64 -> 97.83 and 25.36 -> 101.1 to the digit. Under the model's own 1 mm rule for adjacent pairs (the horn-link 1b pair), all 374 taken poses fail (verifier strict_1mm), so 97.83 is the lenient reading. No spring-return or dynamics number exists for this drive. The dog is one-sided: link 2's flank pushes the sector only while K opens. On the way back, K's spiral spring (the lead's) has to back-drive horn -> drag link -> Ti arm -> sector through the 4R. It works against the sector's turn on hub 2's housing and 4 MR63ZZ, with transmission angles down to 54.5 deg (pa_max_taken 35.5 deg; table end at PA 42). If the return lags, K lags q2 and the cuff twists or the chain binds (G3). Nothing on file measures it: no R17 / judge/dynamics.py run and no CAD for this design. The row's 'R17 ok' covers only static determinacy (with K on stop A, the 4R parks the ring). This is the same open measurement as the lead's M5, which its skeptic upheld as missing. The held-out fold margin is held by the stop only if K is on its law, and the built drive lags. The 5 deg rule reads th, and the J2 stop sits on J2's own angle. th also moves with K, about 0.08 deg of margin per deg of K. The red team measured the as-built drive's systematic K lag at -0.42 to -0.53 deg (arm compliance, follower clearance, wear), with +-0.24 deg random on top. At a lag of -0.1 / -0.5 / -0.7 deg the held-out minimum is 4.998 / 4.966 / 4.950 deg, with 1-2 of 852 taken poses under 5. The bench holds: 5.12 at -0.7 deg, 0 poses under 5. So the rule 'stops engage at >= 5 deg of th in every state' fails by at most 0.05 deg as built without compensation. The verified bench 18.49 does not lean on it; at most 2 held-out poses (<= 0.21 held-out points) do. The fix is in hand: a +0.75 deg K lead (lobe-ring dowel phase +0.35 deg of q2) gives >= 5.003 held out at the worst build. It is in the gen-7 full-CAD builder (pipeline/conformal/param_cad, 'O1 dowel key at the onset phase + 0.35 deg of q2') but not in the judged L1 (no match in pipeline/concept_l1/build_slipper_l1.py or the L1 design.json). judgement:T3: The held-out fold margin is held by the stop only if K is on its law, and the built drive lags. The 5 deg rule reads th, and the J2 stop sits on J2's own angle. th also moves with K, about 0.08 deg of margin per deg of K. The red team measured the as-built drive's systematic K lag at -0.42 to -0.53 deg (arm compliance, follower clearance, wear), with +-0.24 deg random on top. At a lag of -0.1 / -0.5 / -0.7 deg the held-out minimum is 4.998 / 4.966 / 4.950 deg, with 1-2 of 852 taken poses under 5. The bench holds: 5.12 at -0.7 deg, 0 poses under 5. So the rule 'stops engage at >= 5 deg of th in every state' fails by at most 0.05 deg as built without compensation. The verified bench 18.49 does not lean on it; at most 2 held-out poses (<= 0.21 held-out points) do. The fix is in hand: a +0.75 deg K lead (lobe-ring dowel phase +0.35 deg of q2) gives >= 5.003 held out at the worst build. It is in the gen-7 full-CAD builder (pipeline/conformal/param_cad, 'O1 dowel key at the onset phase + 0.35 deg of q2') but not in the judged L1 (no match in pipeline/concept_l1/build_slipper_l1.py or the L1 design.json). The lead's own effect on skin distance and on the score is not measured: a 0.2-0.75 deg K offset moves link 1b's far end by about 0.2-0.8 mm. judgement:NEW-synthesis-cliff: The verified flank sits within manufacturing distance of a re-synthesis cliff, but the score does not stand on it. The final polish's robustness scan of the verified config (priced, Bench(60,160), one at a time) fails 3 of 6 neighbours. beta -1 deg, r_c -0.25 mm and g -0.05 each push the crank pressure angle past its 38.03 deg cap (38.8 / 40.2 / 49.0), and the re-synthesised drive ends at dK 0 (fit near-touch 14.25 -> 86.1). The finer scan puts the edge at r_c -0.20 mm and g -0.02. The fit sample alone moves the crank PA from 29.5 to 38.0. So the CMA left the crank side about 0.2 mm from an immovable drive (T4: the optimum sits against a transmission cap). It is not a knife-edge score, though. The flank-robustness agent's pre-registered beta steps (WIP, verified protocol, unpriced) read 18.48 / 18.46 / 18.44 / 18.43 / 18.70 at beta -175.684 .. -171.684, against 18.49 at -176.684. -174.684, -173.684 and -172.684 pass all 6 neighbours. A robust flank therefore costs 0.03-0.06 points; the verified 18.49 is not bought by sitting on the cliff. Open: whether the BUILT crank (flank fixed, crank off by tolerance) loses stroke is the as-built question, being measured in docs/research/slipper_flank_robust/asbuilt.py; no output yet.
